name: Titanium Yellow
lede: Titanium yellow is a pigment name that books use for more than one thing: a light lemon yellow built from nickel, antimony and titanium oxides, or, in older sources, a yellow made from a titanium ore.

sections.title: Two meanings
sections.body:
The Pigment Compendium records the disagreement: de Keijzer (1990) says titanium yellow was derived from the titanium ore ilmenite, while Hackman (1973) lists it as a synonym for nickel titanate yellow [1]. Mayer (1991) lists nickel titanate yellow and nickel titanium yellow as different things, without saying how they differ [2].

Books disagree, then, on what the name covers. The nickel reading is the one that modern pigment references describe in detail.

sections.title: The nickel rutile yellow
sections.body:
Buxbaum (1998) describes it as a light lemon yellow, a mixed oxide of titanium, antimony and nickel with an approximate formula of (Ti0.85Sb0.10Ni0.05)O2 [2]. He calls it nickel rutile yellow, a name that points to rutile, one of the mineral forms of titanium oxide [2]. Other trade names are sun yellow and titan yellow [2][3].

It is a different compound from the white of the same element, which has its own tangle of names, permanent white among them [4]. In modern paints, chromium and nickel titanium yellows also stand in for the lead antimony oxide of Naples yellow [5].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch is a library entry taken from Wikipedia's color lists, a vivid greenish lemon yellow, and its nearest named neighbor is [[canary]], about three CIEDE2000 units away [6]. A screen cannot show the soft, light lemon that the pigment sources describe, so treat the swatch as a label, not a match [2][6].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Within six units of this yellow, covering at least five per cent of the canvas, our archive finds exactly one painting in 23,781: Mondrian's *Composition in Red, Yellow and Blue* (1922), where it takes about ten per cent [7]. One painting is an anecdote, not a pattern, and these are photographs of varnished paint, not pigment tests [7].

questions.q: Which element's oxides, with nickel and antimony, make the light lemon yellow sold as titanium yellow?
True or false: all sources agree on what 'titanium yellow' means.

openers: The name titanium yellow means an ilmenite-derived color to some authors and a nickel oxide mix to others.
